sex.evidence: Adult male C57BL/6N mice (Charles Rivers, Saint-Constant, Quebec, Canada) (n = 53)

dosing.evidence: LSD (Sigma-Aldrich, London, UK) was dissolved in a 0.9% NaCl vehicle (VEH) solution and administered intraperitoneally (i.p.) ... for 7 days (30 µg/kg/day)

group_housing.evidence: housed under standard laboratory conditions (max 5 per cage)

assays.assay_description: After 10 min habituation, a novel weight- and sex-matched conspecific was introduced into the cage with the test mouse and the mice freely interacted for 10 min. Interaction time (nose-to-anogenital sniffing, nose-to-nose sniffing, social grooming), rearing events, rearing time, grooming bouts and total grooming time were manually scored.

setup_habituation.evidence: After 10 min habituation, a novel weight- and sex-matched conspecific stranger mouse was introduced into the cage

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were able to freely engage in social interaction

food_restriction.evidence: No food placed in the test arena during the 10-min interaction; home cage had ad libitum food.

water_restriction.evidence: No water placed in the test arena during the 10-min interaction; home cage had ad libitum water.

time_to_assay.evidence: The direct social interaction (DSI) test took place 24 h after the 7th injection

sample_size.evidence: VEH (n = 16) or LSD (n = 17); n = 16-17 per group

outcomes.summary: Repeated LSD (30 µg/kg/day, 7 days, i.p.) increased social interaction time with a stranger mouse compared to vehicle. Rearing events, rearing time, grooming bouts and total grooming time were unchanged.
outcomes.statistics: Mann-Whitney test, P < 0.05; unpaired t tests for rearing/grooming (ns).
outcomes.evidence: mice receiving repeated LSD spent significantly more time in social interaction with a stranger mouse in the direct social interaction test compared to VEH-treated mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: interaction time, number of rearing events, rearing time, grooming bouts, total grooming time

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Behaviour reported as totals over the 10-min session.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences/transitions reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: nose-to-anogenital sniffing, nose-to-nose sniffing and social grooming

B5_social.evidence: mice were able to freely engage in social interaction for 10 min

B6_cognitive.evidence: Test does not require learning or memory.

E1_environment_type.evidence: a novel ... stranger mouse was introduced into the cage with the test mouse

E2_shelter.evidence: No enclosed refuge described during the DSI test.

E3_bedding.evidence: Test performed in the home cage which contained nesting material (cages enriched with nesting material).

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects beyond nesting material reported.

E6_spatial.evidence: Home cage is a single compartment.

E7_social_context.evidence: novel conspecific stranger mouse was introduced into the cage with the test mouse and the mice were able to freely engage in social interaction

E8_food_water.evidence: Test conducted in the home cage where food and water are available ad libitum.

D2_session_duration.evidence: freely engage in social interaction for 10 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: DSI performed on a single day, 24 h after the 7th injection.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline behavioural recording reported for this assay.

D5_followup.evidence: The DSI test took place 24 h after the 7th injection

assays.assay_description: Three-chamber social preference/novelty test. Phase 1: 10 min free habituation to empty arena. Phase 2: 10 min with Stranger 1 (S1) under a wire cage vs empty cage (sociability). Phase 3: 10 min with S1 vs a new Stranger 2 (S2) (social novelty). Time spent sniffing, sociability and social novelty indices, and distance travelled were measured.

setup_habituation.evidence: Test mice were placed in the middle chamber and allowed to freely explore the empty three-chamber arena for 10 min

setup_restrain.evidence: test mouse was allowed to explore the three-chamber arena

food_restriction.evidence: No food in the testing arena during the test.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in the testing arena during the test.

time_to_assay.evidence: the three chambers test (TCT) was performed 24 h later [after the 8th injection]

outcomes.summary: Repeated LSD increased the time spent interacting with S1 vs empty cage and with S2 vs S1, and increased the social preference and social novelty indices, without altering locomotion.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc (treatment × sociability significant); unpaired t test for social preference index (P<0.05); Mann-Whitney for social novelty index (P<0.05); RM ANOVA for distance travelled (ns).
outcomes.evidence: LSD-treated mice spent significantly more time interacting with a stranger mouse compared to VEH-treated controls ... LSD-treated mice spent significantly more time interacting with the novel intruder than VEH-treated mice

B1_num_measures.evidence: time sniffing S1/empty/S2, sociability index, social novelty index, distance travelled

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Totals per phase reported; no within-session time-course.

B4_ethological.evidence: time spent sniffing S1, S2 or the empty cage was manually scored

B5_social.evidence: unfamiliar mouse ... was introduced into one of the two side chambers, enclosed in a wire cage, thus allowing only the test mouse to initiate social interaction

B6_cognitive.evidence: social novelty phase requires recognition of S1 as familiar vs S2 as novel (social recognition memory).

E2_shelter.evidence: No enclosed refuge in the three-chamber arena.

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding described in the three-chamber apparatus.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in the three-chamber apparatus.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects in the apparatus.

E6_spatial.evidence: three-chamber arena with side chambers and middle chamber

E7_social_context.evidence: unfamiliar mouse ... enclosed in a wire cage

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water in the three-chamber apparatus.

D1_continuity.evidence: Three sequential 10-min phases (habituation, sociability, social novelty) each recorded.

D3_recording_days.evidence: TCT performed on a single day.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline recorded for the TCT.

D5_followup.evidence: TCT performed 24 h after the 8th injection

judge_notes: Two assays identified: Direct Social Interaction (DSI) and Three Chambers Test (TCT). All candidates agreed on these.

DSI test is conducted in the home cage of the test mouse (paper: 'introduced into the cage with the test mouse'), so E1=Home cage and bedding/nesting/food-water are scored Yes accordingly (per glm and gptoss); qwen's classification as standard apparatus was rejected.
B6 (cognitive) scored 1 for TCT because the social novelty phase requires recognition memory (familiar S1 vs novel S2); scored 0 for DSI which does not require learning.
B5 for DSI = Free social interaction (score 3); B5 for TCT = Restricted (score 2, wire cup).
D1 for TCT scored 1 (multiple discrete phases within session, consistent with gptoss); D5 followup = Yes for both assays since testing occurs 24h after last injection.
